topics: Introduction to Algorithm Design and Analysis
Finding the Median of Merged Arrays

algorithms.name: Algorithm for Maximum Diners
algorithms.description: This algorithm finds the maximum number of diners at any given time by tracking entry and exit points.

algorithms.name: Median of Merged Sorted Arrays
algorithms.description: This algorithm finds the median of two sorted arrays by recursively eliminating half of the elements based on median comparisons.

algorithms.name: Game Strategy for Rami and Dina
algorithms.description: This algorithm determines if Rami has a winning strategy in a game played on a graph by analyzing possible moves and outcomes.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Correctness of Algorithms
theorems_and_concepts.description: An algorithm is correct if it produces the expected output for all valid inputs.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Time Complexity
theorems_and_concepts.description: Time complexity describes the amount of time an algorithm takes to complete as a function of the length of the input.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Asymptotic Notation
theorems_and_concepts.description: Asymptotic notation provides a way to describe the limiting behavior of a function, particularly in terms of time complexity.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Stirling's Approximation
theorems_and_concepts.description: Stirling's approximation provides a formula for approximating factorials, useful in complexity analysis.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Graph Representation in Games
theorems_and_concepts.description: Graphs can be used to represent states and transitions in games, allowing for analysis of winning strategies.

algorithms.name: Merge Sort
algorithms.description: A recursive algorithm that divides the array into two halves, sorts them recursively, and merges the sorted halves.

algorithms.name: Maximum Profit Problem
algorithms.description: An algorithm that finds the optimal days to buy and sell stock to maximize profit using a divide and conquer approach.

algorithms.name: Fast Exponentiation
algorithms.description: An algorithm that computes a^b efficiently by reducing the exponent b by half at each step.

algorithms.name: Majority Element
algorithms.description: An algorithm that determines if there is an element that appears more than half the time in a list using a divide and conquer strategy.

algorithms.name: Huffman Coding
algorithms.description: An algorithm that encodes text using variable-length binary codes based on the frequency of characters to minimize the total length of the encoded text.

algorithms.name: Closest Pair Problem
algorithms.description: An algorithm that finds the contiguous subarray with the largest sum by dividing the array and combining results.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Base Case in Recursion
theorems_and_concepts.description: The condition under which the recursion stops, typically when the problem size is reduced to a trivial case.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Recursive Complexity Analysis
theorems_and_concepts.description: The method of analyzing the time complexity of recursive algorithms using recurrence relations.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Transitivity of Equality
theorems_and_concepts.description: A property that states if a = b and b = c, then a = c, which can reduce the number of comparisons in algorithms.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Prefix-Free Codes
theorems_and_concepts.description: A property of coding schemes where no code is a prefix of another, ensuring unique decodability.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Optimal Substructure
theorems_and_concepts.description: A property of a problem that can be broken down into smaller subproblems, which can be solved independently.

algorithms.name: Greedy Coin Change Algorithm
algorithms.description: Selects the largest coin denomination that does not exceed the remaining amount until the target amount is reached.

algorithms.name: Greedy Interval Scheduling Algorithm
algorithms.complexity: O(n log n) for sorting, O(n) for processing
algorithms.description: Selects intervals that finish first to maximize the number of non-overlapping intervals scheduled.

algorithms.name: Greedy Set Cover Algorithm
algorithms.description: Selects the largest set covering the most uncovered elements until all elements are covered.

algorithms.name: Greedy Minimum Vertex Cover Algorithm on Trees
algorithms.description: Removes leaves from the tree and adds their parent to the vertex cover until all edges are covered.

algorithms.name: Greedy Carpenter Algorithm
algorithms.description: Chooses the farthest cutting point that does not exceed the maximum length allowed.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Greedy Choice Property
theorems_and_concepts.description: A greedy algorithm makes a locally optimal choice at each stage with the hope of finding a global optimum.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Optimal Substructure
theorems_and_concepts.description: An optimal solution to a problem contains optimal solutions to its subproblems.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Proof by Comparison
theorems_and_concepts.description: Compares the greedy algorithm's choices with those of any other algorithm to show that the greedy choice is at least as good.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Proof by Exchange
theorems_and_concepts.description: Shows that an optimal solution can be transformed into a greedy solution without losing optimality.

topics: Heaviest Independent Set in a Path Graph

algorithms.name: Fibonacci Recursive Algorithm
algorithms.description: A recursive algorithm to compute the nth Fibonacci number, which suffers from exponential time complexity due to repeated calculations.

algorithms.name: Dynamic Programming for Fibonacci
algorithms.description: An optimized approach to compute Fibonacci numbers by storing previously computed values to avoid redundant calculations.

algorithms.name: Heaviest Path in a Grid
algorithms.description: An algorithm to find the maximum weight path from the top-left to the bottom-right of a grid, allowing only right and down movements.

algorithms.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
algorithms.description: An algorithm to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence in an array using dynamic programming.

algorithms.name: Heaviest Independent Set in a Path Graph
algorithms.description: An algorithm that computes the maximum weight independent set in a path graph using dynamic programming principles.

algorithms.name: Minimum Vertex Cover on Trees
algorithms.description: An algorithm to find the minimum vertex cover in a tree by recursively calculating the minimum cover for each subtree.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Dynamic Programming
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems and storing the results to avoid redundant calculations.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Exponential Time Complexity
theorems_and_concepts.description: A situation where the time complexity of an algorithm grows exponentially with the input size, often due to repeated calculations.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Recursive Tree Analysis
theorems_and_concepts.description: An analysis method that visualizes the recursive calls of an algorithm as a tree structure to understand its complexity.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Induction Proof
theorems_and_concepts.description: A mathematical proof technique used to establish the truth of a statement for all natural numbers by proving it for a base case and an inductive step.

topics: Longest Path in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)

algorithms.name: Minimum Vertex Cover on Trees
algorithms.description: An algorithm that finds the minimum vertex cover in a tree using dynamic programming by calculating two values for each node: the minimum number of nodes in the cover when the node is included and when it is not.

algorithms.name: Longest Path in a DAG
algorithms.description: An algorithm that computes the longest path in a directed acyclic graph by processing nodes in topological order and maintaining the longest path lengths.

algorithms.name: Edit Distance
algorithms.description: An algorithm that calculates the minimum number of operations required to convert one string into another using a dynamic programming table.

algorithms.name: Tile Tiling Problem
algorithms.description: An algorithm that determines the number of ways to tile a 2xn room using L and I tiles, using recursive relations to build up solutions.

algorithms.name: Diameter of a Tree
algorithms.description: An algorithm that finds the diameter of a tree by calculating the maximum distance between any two nodes, typically using depth-first search.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Vertex Cover
theorems_and_concepts.description: A vertex cover of a graph is a set of vertices such that every edge in the graph is incident to at least one vertex in the set.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Dynamic Programming
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems and storing the results of these subproblems to avoid redundant computations.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Longest Path in a DAG
theorems_and_concepts.description: The longest path in a directed acyclic graph can be found using dynamic programming techniques, leveraging the properties of topological ordering.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Levenshtein Distance
theorems_and_concepts.description: A metric for measuring the difference between two sequences by counting the minimum number of single-character edits required to change one word into the other.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Tiling Problem
theorems_and_concepts.description: A combinatorial problem that involves counting the number of ways to cover a given area with specified shapes, often solved using recursive relations.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Tree Diameter
theorems_and_concepts.description: The diameter of a tree is the longest path between any two nodes in the tree, which can be found using depth-first search techniques.

topics: Shortest paths in directed weighted graphs
Using a specific edge in shortest paths
Shortest path with limited edge weights

algorithms.name: Bellman-Ford
algorithms.description: Used to find the shortest path from a single source in graphs with negative weights.

algorithms.name: Dijkstra's Algorithm
algorithms.description: An efficient algorithm for finding the shortest paths from a source vertex to all other vertices in a graph with non-negative weights.

algorithms.name: BFS for binary matrix multiplication
algorithms.description: Used to multiply binary matrices by constructing a specific graph and running BFS.

algorithms.name: Binary Search for minimum edge weight
algorithms.description: Involves running BFS to find the minimum edge weight L for which a path exists between two vertices.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Shortest Path with Specific Edge
theorems_and_concepts.description: Every path from u to v that passes through a specific edge can be expressed as a combination of optimal paths to and from that edge.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Matrix Multiplication with APSP
theorems_and_concepts.description: Using an APSP algorithm to multiply binary matrices by transforming the problem into a graph traversal problem.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Zigzag Path Concept
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method to find the shortest path that alternates colors between edges, achieved by duplicating the graph.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Limited Edge Weight Concept
theorems_and_concepts.description: A strategy to ignore edges exceeding a certain weight limit and find the shortest path using modified graph traversal.

algorithms.name: BFS
algorithms.description: An algorithm for traversing or searching tree or graph data structures.

algorithms.name: Topological Sorting
algorithms.description: An ordering of the vertices in a directed acyclic graph such that for every directed edge u -> v, vertex u comes before v.

algorithms.name: Dynamic Programming for DAG
algorithms.description: Counts the number of paths from node u to node v in a directed acyclic graph.

algorithms.name: BFS on Layered Graph
algorithms.description: Finds the shortest even-length path from source s to each vertex v in the original graph.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Dynamic Programming
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Graph Representation
theorems_and_concepts.description: Methods to represent graphs, such as adjacency matrices and adjacency lists.

theorems_and_concepts.name: DAG
theorems_and_concepts.description: A directed graph that has no cycles.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Counting Paths in a DAG
theorems_and_concepts.description: Finding the number of distinct paths between two vertices in a directed acyclic graph.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Topological Sorting
theorems_and_concepts.description: A linear ordering of vertices in a directed acyclic graph.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Monotonic Paths
theorems_and_concepts.description: Paths in a DAG that are strictly increasing.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Induction Principle
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method of mathematical proof used to establish the validity of a statement for all natural numbers.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Layered Graph Construction
theorems_and_concepts.description: A method to create a new graph by duplicating nodes to facilitate finding even-length paths.

algorithms.name: Kruskal’s Algorithm
algorithms.description: The algorithm maintains a forest that spans the original graph, starting with n trees, each containing a single vertex and no edges, and adds edges based on their weights.

algorithms.name: Prim’s Algorithm
algorithms.description: The algorithm starts from an arbitrary vertex and adds edges to the minimum spanning tree based on the edges leading from the visited vertices.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Minimum Spanning Tree
theorems_and_concepts.description: A spanning tree of a connected graph with the minimum sum of edge weights.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Cut Property
theorems_and_concepts.description: For any cut in the graph, the lightest edge crossing the cut is part of the minimum spanning tree.

theorems_and_concepts.name: Cycle Property
theorems_and_concepts.description: In a weighted graph with distinct edge weights, the heaviest edge in any cycle cannot be part of the minimum spanning tree.

theorems_and_concepts.name: יחודיות של העץ הפורש המינימלי
theorems_and_concepts.description: הוכחה לכך שלגרף שבו משקל כל קשת הינו יחודי, יש עץ פורש יחיד.
